keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Kalachuri row. The page states no area: it says the dynasty "ruled present-day Maharashtra, as well as parts of mainland Gujarat and southern Madhya Pradesh", with the Konkan and Vidarbha succeeded from the Traikutakas and the Vakatakas. The researcher's regions. Cliopatria draws Vidarbha as Vakataka to 554 and leaves the rest as Chalukya from 555 (156 of 2,688 Vakataka cells, per the sa-02-d notes).

region.text: Mahishmati in the Malwa region on the Narmada

ledger.note: c. 550: Krishnaraja founds the Kalachuri power at Mahishmati. "Krishnaraja (r. c. 550-575) is the earliest known Kalachuri ruler"; around 550 "Malwa lacked a strong ruler, Vakataka rule in Maharashtra had ended, and Maitraka power in Gujarat was declining." The infobox gives no dates; its ruler list runs from 550 to 625.
c. 550: the Kalachuris take northern Konkan. "Konkan was taken by the mid-6th century, succeeding the Traikutakas" (page); the Traikutaka dossier ends c. 550.

region.text: Vidarbha, passed "from the Vakatakas and Vishnukundinas"

ledger.note: c. 550: Vidarbha passes to the Kalachuris. "Vidarbha passed to them from the Vakatakas and Vishnukundinas"; the page gives no date, and the Vakataka dossier ends c. 510 (sa-02-d).

c. 597: Shankaragana takes Ujjain. "took Ujjain around 597 from Mahasenagupta"; a 597 CE inscription issued from Ujjain records a grant near Abhona. A footnote dates "the Maitraka loss of Ujjain to 616-617", which the page does not reconcile.

c. 608: Buddharaja takes Vidisha. "he took Vidisha around 608"; a footnote dates the occupation of Vidisha to 608-609; grants of 609-611 are issued from his camps at Vidisha and Anandapura. The page does not say who held Vidisha.

ledger.note: c. 625: the Kalachuri rule ends under Chalukya pressure. "Buddharaja's reign ended sometime before 630 CE, when Chalukya inscriptions show control of the Nashik area"; the infobox ruler list ends 625; Mangalesha attacked from the south in Buddharaja's reign and Pulakeshin II (possibly his nephew) is also linked to the defeat, with no dates. The Kalachuris were Chalukya feudatories by 687.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks (named as successor in the vakataka-kingdom, traikutaka-dynasty and aulikara-dynasty dossiers; sa-02-d suggested sa-03). One page opened (budget 2-5). The page is dated only by the ruler list (c. 550-625); the occupation of Ujjain (597) and Vidisha (608) are the page's "around" dates, and the Maitraka loss of Ujjain (616-617) in a footnote contradicts the 597 conquest. The Aulikara successor line (aulikara-dynasty ends 545) is not stated by the page, which does not mention the Aulikaras: Malwa "lacked a strong ruler" around 550. Later Gupta counterpart (Mahasenagupta) has no dossier yet (sa-03). Overlap: sa-03 may also write this dossier; keep whichever validates. Gazetteer names needed: Mahishmati, Vidisha, Anandapura (used as radii).
